The Bandung edition is programming 203 international titles drawn from 69 countries. Cristian Mungiu's “ Fjord ,” which won this year's Palme d'Or at Cannes, opened proceedings.

Also on the slate are Beth de Araujo's “Josephine,” which took both the Grand Jury Prize and the Audience Award in Sundance's U.S. Dramatic Competition in 2026, and Marine Atlan's “La Gradiva,” winner of the AMI Paris Grand Prize at this year's Cannes Critics' Week. Sandra Wollner's “Everytime,” which picked up the Un Certain Regard Prize at Cannes, screens alongside Kurosawa Kiyoshi's new feature “The Samurai and the Prisoner,” a Cannes Premiere selection.

The festival's online program, available until Nov. 21, includes Ildiko Enyedi's “Silent Friend,” a Fipresci Prize winner at Venice in 2025, and Ilker Çatak's “Yellow Letters,” this year's Golden Bear winner at the Berlinale.

Bandung Mayor Muhammad Farhan attended the opening night at CGV Paris Van Java.

“Bandung World Cinema gives the local audience an unprecedented opportunity to watch alternative cinema outside of the mainstream Hollywood films that dominate the theaters. In the closing moments of the sketch, former " SNL " trouper Yang walked in delivering a pitch-perfect spoof of Huang, who was forced under pressure to resign on Nov. 12 from the Silicon Valley giant that he built for more than 30 years amid a growing sex scandal. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories 'Hamnet' Play From Royal Shakespeare Company Sets First U.K. Tour

Yang introduced himself "Jensen Hide-Your-Wife Huang." Yang as Huang lamented that "women don't like guys like us. Yang also quipped that when Huang comes into the room, "You know what's about to go down — the S&P 500." And in a nod to Nvidia's heft in the stock market, he added: “That's right — I'm in to BDSM: Breaking the stock market.”

articles.title: Laurence Fishburne Is the Biggest Marvel Fan Who Hasn't Gotten the Great Comic Book Role He Deserves
articles.summary: Laurence Fishburne’s work as Morpheus in The Matrix trilogy would itself be enough to make him an icon of genre entertainment even without his other notable performances in beloved science fiction, fantasy, and horror projects. But while he’s also been part of several onscreen superhero stories, his roles in these projects have not taken full […]
articles.content:
Fishburne previously explained to ComicBook how he became an avid reader of Marvel Comics at the age of six, specifically appreciating how the franchise represented the city of New York, where he grew up, and the inclusion of realistic, relatable themes and social commentary amidst the fantastical stories. In that interview, Fishburne also reiterated his interest in playing new characters in the MCU even though he’s already a part of the franchise, indicating that he may not be entirely satisfied with the acting work he’s already done in comic book adaptations, though he also expressed admiration for the casting of most existing Marvel films.

Fishburne’s first Marvel project was the 2008 film Fantastic Four: Rise of the Silver Surfer , in which he voiced the titular character, also known as Norrin Radd, while Doug Jones performed the Surfer’s physical role. The Fantastic Four comic was at the height of its popularity during Fishburne’s 1960s childhood, and the storyline the film is based on, which introduced both the Surfer and his villainous master, Galactus, is one of the most revered in comics history, which likely influenced a fan like Fishburne to take the role. Unfortunately, while some opinions on the 2005 Fantastic Four film have softened over time, the sequel continues to be panned, though Fishburne’s performance is often cited as one of its more significant redeeming qualities.

After portraying Daily Planet editor Perry White in the DC Extended Universe films Man of Steel and Batman v. Superman: Dawn of Justice , Fishburne joined the MCU in 2018’s Ant-Man and the Wasp . He portrayed Bill Foster, a colleague of scientist Hank Pym’s (Michael Douglas) who had also covertly worked as a size-changing superhero for the espionage agency S.H.I.E.L.D., during which time he used the code name “Goliath,” like his comics counterpart. After growing estranged from Hank, Bill became an adoptive father to Ava Starr/Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen,) the daughter of another of Bill and Hank’s colleagues whose parents were both killed in an experiment that left her with superpowers, chronic pain, and limited time to live. While Ava initially worked as an assassin for S.H.I.E.L.D. in exchange for a containment suit that stabilized her condition and the promise of an eventual cure, when she and Bill realized the agency, which was still largely controlled by the Nazi organization Hydra at the time, had no intention of making good on that promise, they went rogue and turned to crime to facilitate Bill’s efforts to cure her.

Although desperate to save Ava, Bill also served as her conscience, with his influence keeping her from ever crossing the line into true villainy. Fishburne returned to voice alternate universe variants of Bill in the second and third seasons of the animated MCU spin-off series What If…? and standalone Marvel comedy series Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur . But while the projects Fishburne’s played the role in have all received at least modestly positive reviews, Bill has yet to gain much popularity from the MCU fan base. It’s possible this could change with future stories, and the character’s chances of reappearing would presumably be at their highest at the current moment, while Ava is serving as a member of the Thunderbolts/New Avengers. But there’s been no indication of whether such a return appearance will actually come to be, and again, some of Fishburne’s own comments imply that he may prefer to take on a different role.

Fishburne specifically expressed interest in playing Charles Xavier in the MCU’s X-Men reboot film , noting that Charles is one of the characters he thinks he would currently be an appropriate age for. But it was announced this summer that younger actor Christopher Abbott will actually be the one to portray the mutant teacher in director Jake Schreier’s 2028 X-Men film. In the past, many actors who have played more than one character in the MCU have had one part where their appearance is recognizable, with the others being characters that are not human or whose appearances are otherwise unique, with the actors either solely providing their voices or portraying them physically but disguised through motion capture and visual effects and/or by elaborate costumes and makeup. An increasing number of actors have also played multiple human characters, but in most cases this has involved them having brief background parts in earlier projects before being cast for larger roles in later ones.

Many fans have speculated that next year’s Avengers: Secret Wars will make some significant changes to the existing MCU continuity. If this is the case and Ava continues to appear in the franchise it’s possible her personal history could be altered, freeing Fishburne to play a different, recognizable character without creating confusion about Bill. Whatever the case, it will be a shame if Fishburne never gets a more memorable onscreen Marvel role, whether that means returning as Bill or the Surfer for more fleshed-out storylines, or by taking on a new character entirely.

articles.title: 5 Future Versions of Superman Who Are Truly Men of Tomorrow
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Superman has always symbolized the best of humanity and how, through hope and kindness, a better tomorrow can be achieved. With his immeasurable power and optimism, Superman ensures that the world never loses hope, even far into the future. As a Kryptonian, Superman ages much slower than normal humans. This slowed aging allows him to […]
articles.content:
Superman was the first hero in DC Comics, and his long lifespan ensures that either he or his successors will continue being the DC Universe’s foremost protectors for centuries to come. For as long as there’s a Superman, there’s still hope.

By the year 3000 in the DC Universe, humanity has become a space-faring civilization that has intermingled with various alien races. However, this time period also was when the supervillain team known as the Five has spread chaos across the cosmos. To fight these villains, Dr. Ariel Masters and the Wonder Twins sought to resurrect the long-dead Justice League through cloning. Using volunteers' bodies, these scientists overrode their DNA so that they’d transform into Justice League clones with the powers, personalities, and memories of the original Leaguers. However, the Superman clone showed significant adverse side effects. Not only could he not fly or shoot lasers from his eyes, but he was also extremely arrogant and brash. Luckily, this imperfect clone of Superman was still enough of a hero to lead the Justice League 3000 to defeat the Five. Yet this victory didn’t stop robot assassins from later killing this Superman. Thankfully, the year 3000 still has a Kryptonian protector in Superman’s cousin, Supergirl.

In the 853rd century, humanity has expanded across the solar system and beyond, with the Justice Legion Alpha as its primary defenders. The leader of this futuristic team is the latest member of the Superman Dynasty, Kal Kent, aka Superman. Known as the Man of Beyond Tomorrow, Kal’s Kryptonian physiology is drastically enhanced by the 853rd century’s Super-Sun. He’s known to be faster than a speeding tachyon, more powerful than the gravitational pull of a collapsing star, and able to leap from world to world in a single bound. Not only that, but one of Kal’s ancestors is a Queen Gzntplkzk of the Fifth Dimension, which led him to inherit potent telepathic abilities along with ten extra senses. When he’s not fighting crime across the universe or leading the Justice Legion, Kal uses 853rd-century time-travel technology to defend the timestream from villains like Solaris and Epoch. With these powers and acts of heroism, Kal continues the proud history of the Superman Dynasty.

One of the most popular depictions of the DC Universe’s future is in the Batman Beyond animated series. And just as the future still needs a Batman, it also needs a Superman. However, unlike Batman, who gave his mantle to Terry McGinnis, Clark Kent is still operating as Superman thanks to his decelerated aging. However, this older version of Superman has dealt with a lot of hardship. For years, Starro the Conqueror secretly mind-controlled him and tried to use him to destroy Justice League Unlimited. But even after being freed from Starro’s brainwashing, Superman struggles to maintain his connection to humanity. Superman became especially detached after the death of his wife, Lois, and the world continues to change around him. However, Superman still tries to retain his connection with humanity by taking on the new identity of firefighter Kal Kent. Now, whether as a superhero or a civilian, Superman saves lives.

The critically acclaimed Elseworlds story Kingdom Come centers on a dark future where heroes from two generations battle for humanity's fate. And one of the main players in this conflict is an older Superman. In the near future, Superman experiences a terrible loss when the Joker kills everyone at the Daily Planet, including Lois Lane. And when the Joker was being sent to jail, the anti-hero Magog killed him, to the roaring approval of the public. This tragic loss of his friends and his wife led Superman to retire for years. However, after a disaster indirectly caused by the next-generation anti-heroes destroyed Kansas, Superman decided to come out of retirement. He reformed the Justice League in order to keep these anti-heroes in check. This decision would ultimately lead to a superhuman civil war that killed dozens of heroes. Afterward, Superman learned to reconnect with his humanity and then settle down and start a family with Wonder Woman, ensuring a brighter future.

The 853rd century may already have plenty of members of the Superman Dynasty flying around protecting the universe, but none of them compares to the raw power of the original Man of Tomorrow. For even one million months into the future, Clark Kent Superman is still very much alive. After the deaths of all his loved ones, Superman would leave Earth at the end of the 21st century and not return until the 700th century. After gaining incredible new abilities during his travels, he passed some of these increased powers on to his descendants. He then spent the next several centuries in his new Fortress of Solitude inside the sun. Unsurprisingly, spending all that time inside a yellow star eventually led to Superman taking on one of his most powerful forms in DC Comics history: Superman Prime. Emerging in the 853rd century, Superman Prime is practically a god , able to resurrect not just Lois, but all of Krypton.

What do you think of these future Supermen? Leave a Comment below and join the conversation in the ComicBook Forum!

articles.title: DC's Young Adult Comics Deserve More Attention, and Its Latest Birds of Prey Graphic Novel Proves Why
articles.summary: Merging DC Ink and DC Zoom in 2020, DC Comics created its most recent imprint targeted towards younger audiences — DC Graphics for Young Adults. Since then, the imprint has consistently brought fan-favorite characters to new readers in easy-to-find, more digestible formats. Since 2020, the imprint has published 38 graphic novels, featuring Kami Gracia’s Teen […]
articles.content:
Most recently, Sara Shephard, author of the cult-classic, best-selling teen series Pretty Little Liars , partnered with artist Stephanie Pepper for Birds of Prey : The Origins. The graphic novel takes readers to Gotham Prep and reintroduces fan favorites Helena Bertinelli (Huntress), Barbara Gordon (Batgirl/Oracle), Dinah Lance (Black Canary), and Harleen Quinzel ( Harley Quinn ). Each girl has a secret—as is typical Shepard fare—that they need to figure out how far they’ll go to keep it that way as strange things start happening to their fellow students.

The mystery story is not only right in Shepard’s wheelhouse, but also keeps the main spirit of the Birds of Prey comics without the baggage of continuity. Birds of Prey , since its inception, has been about clashing values and putting differences aside.

The team originally started with a one-shot by Chuck Dixon, featuring a post- Killing Joke Barbara Gordon acting as the woman in the chair, with Dinah Lance as a field operative. Writer Gail Simone added Bertinelli’s Huntress to the lineup in the 2000s, while Harley Quinn wouldn't be added until much later.

Some of DC’s most iconic stories have been graphic novels — they’re longer than typical comics, and unlike the usual fare, they are self-contained and can be understood without knowing the larger context. In 1987, DC put out their first standalone graphic novel for Batman, titled Batman: Son of the Demon. Son of the Demon was immensely popular and was beloved by fans. The comic was quickly declared out of continuity, and by the ‘90s, editorial decided that the matter of Talia and Bruce’s son — whom Grant Morrison would revisit and name Damian Wayne — was off the table and not to be touched.

Batman: Son of the Demon , along with other successful Batman graphic novels, paired with the success of DC’s Black Label line — established in 2018 — makes out-of-continuity graphic novels a no-brainer. They sell, and they can push the character in a new direction while still allowing for the toys to be reset in the sandbox by the end of the story. New readers can get to know beloved characters beyond what they’re seen in TV and film adaptations.

Despite being standalone stories for the most part, DC Graphics for Young Adults has still been able to launch interconnected graphic novels. Starting as a carryover from DC Ink, Kami Garcia’s Teen Titans series includes not only the 2018 Teen Titans: Raven but five other graphic novels, with the last installment, Teen Titans: Together, published in 2026. The series proved sufficiently popular with readers to launch a sequel series about the Young Justice Team, with the first installment in that series set to feature Kid Flash and Blue Beetle.

One of the two main stars of DC’s Pride Summer event, Galaxy was first introduced in Galaxy: The Prettiest Star back in May 2022. By April 2023, the graphic novel had nearly sold out, and DC sent it for a second printing. Galaxy later joined Axelrod’s run on Hawkgirl and was a major character in the graphic novel Bad Dream: A Dreamer Story before later joining the Justice League.

DC ’s Young Adult comics are not afraid of the teen coming-of-age genre. It has embraced it for heroes and villains alike, spotlighting Pamela Isley in Poison Ivy: Thorns and the much underappreciated but totally awesome twin sister of Wonder Woman in Nubia: Real One. Mister Miracle: The Great Escape reimagines Scott Free’s romance with Big Barda, and Constantine: Distorted Illusions finds the skilled magician as the lead singer of a punk band.

Birds of Prey: The Origins is undoubtedly a coming-of-age story, but its gestures towards mystery could very well be indicative of where the imprint should go next. Literature aimed at teenagers often goes a coming-of-age route, but after a while, it can feel formulaic. It can be successful, but also get creatively stale.

Leaning into mystery, horror, or other genres outside the typical teen coming-of-age could be the next phase for DC Graphics for Young Adults. Birds of Prey , in the tradition of Teen Titans and the upcoming Young Justice books, has the makings of a team book, one that could spin off into a series. Gotham, even in the world of Birds of Prey: The Origins , is not without its secrets and intrigue.

What other directions should DC Young Adult Comics go in, or is the tried-and-true formula working for them? Let us know in the comments!

articles.title: Ebenezer Audiences Defy Rotten Tomatoes Score to Prove Johnny Depp Is Still A Box Office Draw
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Paramount Pictures Johnny Depp's return to Hollywood studio filmmaking in Ebenezer has become a popular move with movie audiences, despite lower Rotten Tomatoes scores. Depp returned to studio movies for the first time since 2018’s Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald, after which Warner Bros. replaced him in the franchise, and Depp took a hiatus from high-profile […]
articles.content:
It looks to be a huge success as well. Directed by Ti West ( X , Pearl ), Ebenezer is a horror-tinged adaptation of A Christmas Carol , and while critics were not as thrilled with it, audiences seem to be loving it. While it has a 53% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes, Ebenezer has a 91% audience score, which is Verified Hot on the Popcornmeter. The Hollywood Reporter also reports that audiences gave it a 4.5 out of 5 on PostTrak, with 50 percent saying Johnny Depp was the reason they went to see the movie.

Johnny Depp's 'Ebenezer' Conjuring Up Box Office Victory in Star's Return to Studio Fare https://t.co/bmxEv1wupG

According to reports, 62% of the audience that saw Ebenezer in its Thursday night opening screenings was over 30. It received an A- CinemaScore from audiences, bucking the critics' trend as well. It seems that audiences were ready to move on from Johnny Depp's controversial past with Amber Heard, in which he was accused of abuse but then won a defamation lawsuit against her based on her accusations. It seemed like it would be hard for Depp to come back, even after winning his case against Heard. However, Paramount saw data suggesting that audiences wanted Depp back.

Ebenezer had made $6.7 million following its Friday screenings, which went along with the positive audience experience. The movie only had a $38 million budget, so things are looking good for the holiday horror movie. It also helps that Ebenezer has a PG-13 rating, allowing a larger audience than most of Ti West's movies, and while its lower Rotten Tomatoes score seemed troubling, it seemed that audiences didn't care and just wanted to see a new Depp movie on the big screen. THR ‘s own review said that the movie restored Depp to A-list status.

Paramount expects Ebenezer to finish its opening weekend at around $20 million, and since it is a Christmas movie with positive audience reception, it is expected to have better legs than non-holiday releases. These numbers were actually higher than The Numbers had predicted, with them coming in about 28% more than expected. This could also be the huge news that will relaunch Johnny Depp's career. There has been talk of Depp returning to the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise , and if Ebenezer is any indication, this should be more likely now than it was before.

Have you been to see Ebenezer in theaters? Let us know your thoughts on the new Johnny Depp movie in the comments below.

articles.title: Star Wars: Starfighter Could Finally Fix the Biggest Franchise Problem With the Sequel Trilogy
articles.summary: Star Wars has a galaxy full of possibilities. You wouldn't know it from watching some of its movies. But Disney keeps digging deeper into past characters and past stories. Don't get me wrong. Seeing Luke Skywalker wield a lightsaber will always be exciting. Both Rogue One and Andor had good reception. And I'm still the […]
articles.content:
That's why Starfighter could be a very important movie for Lucasfilm. It has an opportunity to leave the family drama behind and introduce audiences to new characters. In my opinion, The Rey trilogy really messed up the original lore with Palpatine, Luke Skywalker, Han Solo, and Leia Organa. It gave us new heroes and then kept reminding us about the old ones—while ruining them. There's a lesson in there for sure. Maybe the best way to make Star Wars exciting again isn't to bring back—and mess up—previous lore, like The Acolyte . Maybe it's time to finally let a new generation take the controls.

The sequel trilogy had some interesting ideas. Rey was a mysterious young woman discovering her connection to the Force. Finn was a stormtrooper who decided he'd rather not spend his life serving a murderous space dictatorship. That's a pretty good premise for a character. Poe Dameron brought the swagger, too. There was plenty to work with. Unfortunately, the movies seemed much more interested in connecting everything to the original trilogy. Rey's journey eventually became tangled up with Palpatine, while Kylo Ren spent much of his time trying to live up to Darth Vader while failing his parents Han and Leia. Even Finn's fascinating background as a former stormtrooper never received the attention it deserved.

Luke got perhaps the worst deal of all. Remember the kid from Tatooine who risked everything because he believed there was still good in Darth Vader? That was the character audiences waited decades to see again. Instead, The Last Jedi presented a bitter Luke who had considered killing his sleeping nephew after sensing darkness in him. I understand that heroes can become disillusioned. That's a perfectly reasonable direction for a story. But watching Luke lose faith in the very people he once refused to abandon was difficult to swallow. It also created an awkward problem for Rey. Her story needed room to develop, yet so much of the trilogy's emotional weight rested on dismantling Luke's legacy. She deserved better than becoming the next chapter in somebody else's family history.

There's a reason the original Star Wars felt so exciting. George Lucas dropped audiences into a universe that seemed to exist long before the opening crawl. We didn't need to know every detail about Obi-Wan Kenobi or Han Solo before meeting them. They had personalities, problems, and their own reasons for getting involved in the adventure. Even Rogue One understood the appeal of telling a story away from the Skywalker family. We knew how the larger story would end, but that didn't stop us from caring about Jyn Erso and her unlikely group of rebels. In some ways, that movie captured the spirit of the original trilogy better than the sequels did.

That's the opportunity sitting in front of Lucasfilm. Starfighter doesn't need another appearance from Luke or a surprise revelation about somebody's ancestry. It needs characters who can hold our attention without borrowing somebody else's legacy. Think about how much of this galaxy we've barely explored. There are entire corners of the Star Wars universe that could support wonderful adventures. Why keep revisiting the same old conflicts? The franchise already has its legends. Now it needs to make some new ones. I'd happily spend two hours following a completely unfamiliar character through a strange corner of the galaxy. Give me a great story, a few memorable characters, and maybe a spaceship that looks like it needs an oil change. Most of all, capture the best elements of cinema from the '70s to '90s. That's Star Wars to me.

articles.title: This 2026 Flop Is Destined to Become a Cult Classic, And Movie History Proves It
articles.summary: Image via WB 2026 has been an odd year at the box office, with some surefire hits from major franchises like the DCU and Star Wars winding up disappointments, while smaller films like Obsession have become box office sensations. Interestingly, one of the biggest box office gambles of the year wound up not paying off, although the story […]
articles.content:
Some of the most popular films of all time are considered cult classics due to their failing upon their initial releases, with movies like Blade Runner , The Shawshank Redemption , Fight Club , and more beginning their lives as disappointments. Based on this trend, I'm sure this 2026 flop will one day be remembered as a classic, and here's why.

Digger Will Inevitably Become A Cult Classic, Despite Being A Box Office Bomb Image via WB Tom Cruise is one of the biggest movie stars working today, which is why the 2026 film Digger was such an interesting experiment. Warner Bros. released Digger with a $180 million budget , and the film's success almost entirely hinged on Cruise's involvement. Its political nature and hard-to-describe plot meant that it was nearly impossible to advertise the film. The vague trailers didn't offer a clear hook to audience members, and the film was a wholly original idea, meaning that Digger ‘s entire marketing campaign centered on the involvement of Cruise as Digger Rockwell.

Unfortunately, this strategy didn't work. Digger has gone on to become one of the biggest box office bombs of all time, with it only making $49 million. The film is estimated to have lost $150-$200 million, and in a year of flops for Warner Bros., Digger is easily the biggest.

However, the film is much more than its box office. Digger is divisive , but it has an incredibly dedicated fanbase that has given it incredible reviews. It is incredibly timely in the modern era of films like Don't Look Up and The Social Reckoning , and its biting satire can be analyzed endlessly. Plus, Cruise's performance is incredible, although this can also be said regarding John Goodman, Sandra Hüller, Riz Ahmed, and the rest of the cast. Digger is Alejandro González Iñárritu at his best, adding another gem to the director's stacked filmography.

Tons of films that were divisive because of their politics have gone on to become cult classics, with movies like Fight Club , The Rocky Horror Picture Show , and Dr. Strangelove or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb finding much larger audiences years after their releases. This is because their predictions have come true and their commentary has become more salient. Digger will likely follow this same path, as more and more audience members get on board with what the film is saying about art's role in politics.

One important factor in Digger becoming a cult classic is that it likely won't be forgotten. The film's association with some of the most popular actors of all time means that it will be frequently mentioned when these performers are discussed. Its box office underperformance will be constantly analyzed for years to come. Plus, the fact that it was Warner Bros.' final release ahead of the Paramount merger means that Digger is historic. All of these factors mean that Digger will have a massive impact on film history, bringing more and more eyes to the film as the years go on.

Another reason that Digger is likely to become a cult classic is that Tom Cruise has already starred in several cult classics throughout his career. Take, for example, 1985's Legend . Although the Cruise-led film made only $23.5 million against a budget of $25 million, it has gone on to become one of the defining examples of '80s fantasy. Similarly, Cruise starred in Stanley Kubrick's 1999 film Eyes Wide Shut , the box office disappointment that has since been reassessed as one of the director's best films.

Cruise's stardom means that anything he appears in is interesting, and Digger will be treated the same way. Fans of Cruise will come back to Digger , fascinated by the oddity of its box office and story. If Digger does well during awards season, more eyes could be brought to the film, further advancing its cult status. Digger is one of the best films of 2026, and I can't imagine that its audience won't grow in the near future.

What did you think of Digger ? Let us know on the ComicBook Forum !

articles.title: Chris Pratt Responds to the Possibility of Guardians 4 After James Gunn Exit
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Chris Pratt said he would love to work with James Gunn again on Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4. With Gunn out of his position as the head of DC Studios, Marvel fans have begun to wonder if there is a chance he could come back for a new Guardians of the Galaxy movie. Gunn […]
articles.content:
In an interview with MovieZine (via The Hollywood Reporter ), Pratt commented on the possibility of reuniting with James Gunn for Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 . “I love working with James [Gunn]. He’s the man. I haven’t had a chance to speak with him since that news came out,” Pratt said. “He directed all three [ Guardians ] movies, and that’s pretty rare in those types of trilogies to have the same director through all three, so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, man, I would love that.”

Chris Pratt “Would Love” to Make a Fourth ‘Guardians of the Galaxy’ Film With James Gunn "If He Wanted to" Amid DC Exit https://t.co/VFTg84i39v

The idea of James Gunn making a new Guardians of the Galaxy movie is unlikely, and even if it happened, it would face a significant change. The last movie ended with Gamora gone, Peter Quill returning to Earth to reunite with his grandfather, and Rocket taking leadership of a new, younger Guardians lineup that includes names like Phyla-Vel and Adam Warlock. A new Guardians movie would have a completely different lineup, and going back to the original would seem to be a step backward.

However, there is a much better use of Peter Quill in the MCU than reuniting him with the Guardians of the Galaxy. Marvel is bringing Richard Rider's Nova to the MCU , and that would easily be the best use of Star-Lord for the future. Star-Lord and Nova are the best of friends in Marvel Comics, and they could end up involved in what could be the most entertaining buddy superhero movie that Marvel has ever made. They could be involved in any sort of superhero movie, from a heist film to something more along the lines of a cosmic war movie. Bringing Star-Lord back to work with Nova could also help lead to an Annihilation movie.

The problem is that James Gunn might not be interested in this. Remember, Gunn didn't bring Richard Rider into his Guardians movies and never seemed interested in that specific relationship. It also seems like Gunn returning to Guardians would be a step backward for the filmmaker. If anything, the changes at DC should allow Gunn to branch out and make something new and interesting, and that will be better than just regurgitating something he did in the past.

articles.title: 4 Dark Fantasy Movies People Have Forgotten About & 1 Is a Twisted Take on a Fairy Tale
articles.summary: There are many ways to explore fantasy, and dark fantasy is one of them: Pan's Labyrinth, Bram Stoker's Dracula, The Dark Crystal, Edward Scissorhands, and The Witch, for example, are some of the most popular and most recommended movies in the genre. But did you know that it also has room for lesser-known productions that […]
articles.content:
In this list, you'll find some of these movies that have found their own ways of mixing magical and supernatural elements with horror and some disturbing ideas, which are very much at the heart of dark fantasy.

Remember Little Red Riding Hood ? When we think of this fairy tale, we obviously picture the child-friendly version in which a girl walks through the forest and comes across a wolf . However, there's a much darker version of the story (released long before the better-known Red Riding Hood from 2011) that explores what the tale might represent rather than just reimagining it. The Company of Wolves blends werewolves, nightmares, and themes of coming of age and sexuality as it follows Rosaleen (Sarah Patterson), a teenage girl who starts dreaming about a mysterious forest while listening to her grandmother's stories about men who hide their true nature and women who end up paying the price for trusting them.

And as these stories begin to overlap with events in the girl's own life, it's hard to tell what's a dream, what's imagination, and what's reality. So it's a more horror-driven take on the classic tale. The werewolves aren't monsters that need to be defeated , but rather a way to explore the fears and discoveries of a young girl who's starting to understand the adult world. The Company of Wolves definitely isn't for anyone looking for something straightforward or clear explanations for everything that happens, but it's certainly one of the best examples of what dark fantasy can mean.

If you're the kind of person who enjoys fantasy films that think outside the box, you may have heard of The City of Lost Children. Its only real flaw is how easily it's been forgotten, because this is a masterpiece that actually gets what fantasy filmmaking can be . Set in a strange universe, the story revolves around Krank (Daniel Emilfork), a scientist who kidnaps children to steal their dreams in the hopes of preventing himself from aging. When Denree (Joseph Lucien), the younger brother of One (Ron Perlman), a strong man, is taken, One teams up with a girl named Miette (Judith Vittet) to try to get him back. But hold on, because the movie goes beyond being just a rescue adventure.

Everything in this universe is eccentric, from its machines to the criminals who inhabit an industrial city that looks nothing like what you'd expect from a more conventional fantasy story ( it also plays around quite a bit with sci-fi elements for that very reason). However, the most important thing is the idea behind Krank's obsession: children's dreams represent something he has lost and is desperately trying to get back at any cost. It's an unusual but fascinating way to explore the fear of aging and the importance of childhood. And well, the narrative can be a little confusing at times, but The City of Lost Children is exactly the kind of movie that reminds you how much we're missing films with this level of creativity.

It's unlikely that you've heard of The Reflecting Skin , but it's a truly intriguing movie since it tells its story through the way a child interprets things he can't quite understand. Here, we meet Seth Dove (Jeremy Cooper), an eight-year-old boy living in a small rural community in the United States during the '50s. After hearing stories about vampires and witnessing violent events, he starts to suspect that his neighbor, Dolphin Blue (Lindsay Duncan), is a creature responsible for the disappearance of children. But things get a little more complicated when his older brother, Cameron (Viggo Mortensen), returns home and becomes involved with the woman, leading Seth to try to convince him that she's dangerous.

Well, it's basically a vampire movie , but it's worth it because, at the same time, it doesn't try to be what you'd expect: there's actually no clear supernatural threat for you to follow, and you have to deal with the same confusion as Seth throughout the story, never really knowing where his imagination ends. So vampirism is actually more of a part of Seth's interpretation of the world, and what really sticks with you after watching The Reflecting Skin is the uncomfortable take on childhood. And there's a bonus: you get to see one of Mortensen's first major roles before he became Aragorn in The Lord of the Rings .

November is an Estonian production with an 81% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. And if there's one movie on this list that's dark fantasy through and through, it's this one. The story takes place in the 19th century, with Liina (Rea Lest) at the center of it all. She's a young woman in love with Hans (Jörgen Liik), who's interested in the daughter of a German baron. As she struggles with this unrequited love, she lives in a community where people will do anything to survive the winter, including making deals with the Devil. And since the movie is based on Estonian folklore, some of the creatures are extremely interesting, such as the kratts: servants made from discarded objects and animal remains that come to life after their creators strike a deal with evil forces.

And the people in this community are always trying to find ways to take advantage of these beings and even trick the Devil himself. So, it's dark fantasy, but also with romance, horror, and humor (the really absurd kind). Still, what's so good about November is that even though it doesn't follow a more common structure and its black-and-white cinematography fits everything perfectly, the combination of strange creatures and the unexpected makes the experience unique. Those who've seen it have nothing but praise. Everything about it is crazy and feels like something straight out of a fairy tale, but one meant for adults in the most brilliant way.

articles.title: ‘Wicker’ Star Alexander Skarsgård Appreciated “Social Commentary” Of Feminist Romantasy Film Without It Being “Too Preachy” - Contenders L.A.
articles.summary: The script — and actress Olivia Colman’s attachment to the project – was the ultimate draw for star Alexander Skarsgård to undergo quite a transformation into the straw-plaited husband of Ursula Wills’ short story-based film Wicker from Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson. “From the first page, I was just immersed in this fantasy, in […]
articles.content:
The script — and actress Olivia Colman's attachment to the project – was the ultimate draw for star Alexander Skarsgård to undergo quite a transformation into the straw-plaited husband of Ursula Wills' short story-based film Wicker from Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson .

"From the first page, I was just immersed in this fantasy, in this fable, in this saga, and I thought it was so funny and romantic and sexy and irreverent with a lot of interesting social commentary on patriarchy and the institution of marriage and jealousy in society and that hierarchy that we that we have in our society and how hard it is to break that," Skarsgård said Saturday during the panel for the film at Deadline Contenders Film Los Angeles event. "But I thought these guys had done it so beautifully, where it never felt too preachy or annoying. ‘Oh, this is the message of the movie.' It was so subtly inserted into the story. At no point was it not entertaining and sweet and funny and crazy." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Pillion star admitted that there were moments he cracked up laughing with Colman, who ultimately was "anti-fuss," according to co-director Fischer.

"They surgically removed those [moments] from the edit," he said. "I'm also wearing a mask. You have no idea what's happening underneath."

The wicker-suit getup was "horrible" to wear, Skarsgård joked.

"We wanted a bit of a journey and evolution for the character, so that stepping into the suit for the first time helped with the finding the physicality of it. We wanted a certain rigidity and stiffness to the character and also the quality of his voice was something we talked a lot about," Skarsgård said. articles.title: DCU Change.org Petition to Reinstate Gunn & Safran Reaches a Big Milestone, & It's 3x #RestoreTheSnyderverse
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Warner Bros There is a new petition on Change.org to reinstate James Gunn and Peter Safran as the co-heads of DC Studios. While it is not likely to make any difference to Skydance and David Ellison, there is one very interesting thing about it. This new petition already has almost three times the number of signatures as […]
articles.content:
The Change.org petition for restoring the SnyderVerse has a total of just over 79,000 verified signatures, and it has been up since January 2021. On the other hand, the Change.org petition for James Gunn and Peter Safran has only been up since November 9, and it already has over 201,000 signatures.

Over 200K and Gunn's still loading. ⁰DC fans are rallying behind James Gunn and Peter Safran after Skydance announced their exit from DC Studios. The petition to keep them has passed 200,000 signatures, with 121,490 of those coming in a SINGLE DAY! 🔗 https://t.co/6yihwUr4Lb pic.twitter.com/oIECiGmP3O

This petition probably won't change anything. David Ellison has clearly been planning to make a change since Skydance started to move forward with its takeover of Warner Bros. There is also the fact that James Gunn openly said that he was ready to get back to just making movies again, rather than running a movie studio. However, it's clear that fans want Gunn and Safran to know where they stand on this. The fact that it is blowing away the smaller number of very vocal Snyderverse fans who signed that petition speaks volumes. It proves that just because one group is very vocal, there might not be as many of them as they might believe.

In the comments on the Change.org petition itself, many fans were very outspoken about why they want Gunn's vision to continue in the DCU . A supporter named David wrote, “The DCU has an incredible amount of potential right now, and I don't believe it's had a single outright bad project thus far. I just want the best for this universe and its storytellers.” Another signee named Naomi wrote, “As a person who’s been a fan of DC for only a couple years, I have been so excited to see all the new characters Gunn was bringing to life! It would truly break my heart to not see it grow to an amazing storyline.”

However, not everyone has been so optimistic about the petition. One commenter on X wrote that the 200,000 people who signed the petition should go watch Clayface because Skydance cares more about the box office than signatures on a petition.

200,000 people should go out and watch Clayface this weekend. That'll do better than this petition because the one thing Skydance is looking at is the box office

James Gunn took over the DCU and has released three movies and three streaming shows. Of the movies, Superman made $618.7 million on a $225 million budget. Supergirl was a box office flop, making only $126.5 million with an estimated budget of over $170 million. Finally, Clayface has brought in $116.6 million and counting on a lower budget of between $30 million and $44 million. Peacemaker earned a Primetime Emmy Award nomination, while Lanterns was one of the most-watched streaming series when it was released earlier this year.

articles.title: Hexed Brings Back One of Disney’s Longest Traditions, and It’s a Genius Move in 2026
articles.summary: Walt Disney Animation Studios has been on an interesting journey over the past decade. 2016 was a record-breaking year for Disney, thanks in large part to the box office success of both Zootopia and Moana. But since then, the studio has leaned more than ever before on sequels. Follow-ups to Wreck-It Ralph, Frozen, Moana, and […]
articles.content:
Truly, 2021’s Encanto is perhaps the only original Disney animated film in recent years to establish a lasting cultural footprint. So the studio has a lot riding on its new film Hexed . The movie dips back into familiar territory, incorporating fairy tale and fantasy elements such as a clandestine magical world, and features the voice talents of stars like Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones, Walton Goggins, Henry Winkler, Dan Stevens, and two-time Oscar winner Jodie Foster. But with Hexed , Disney is also turning to a tried-and-true tactic to lure audiences to theaters.

Dating back to 1928’s Steamboat Willie , Disney animated shorts have been playing in theaters ahead of new movies. The creation of these shorts, of course, predates the first full-length animated film, Disney’s 1937 film Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs . And over the years, the studio has often paired its theatrical features with short films. This even extended past its animated films to live-action movies bearing the Disney brand. Of course, Disney isn’t the only studio to apply this tactic, but seeing how synonymous the company behind Mickey Mouse is with pioneering and popularizing animated storytelling, it’s always notable when Disney debuts a new animated short.

Over the past few decades, Disney has sporadically kept this longtime tradition alive, as has Pixar Animation Studios . However, Disney’s commitment to debuting new animated short films in theaters has waned in recent years. In fact, its most recent theatrically released animated short was Far from the Tree , which was attached to the release of Encanto in late 2021. However, the release of Hexed marks a welcome return to the beloved Disney tradition of preceding a new film with a brand-new animated short. And this time, audiences can look forward to the return of a fan-favorite character.

Screenings of Hexed will include a new animated short set within the popular Lilo & Stitch franchise. Set soon after the original 2002 film, Lilo & Scratch sees Stitch — voiced once again by Chris Sanders, co-director of the original animated film and the sequel to the 2025 live-action adaptation — come up against a mischievous cat that Lilo adopts, the titular Scratch. For the short, Maia Kealoha reprises her role as Lilo from the 2025 live-action Lilo & Stitch . The short features a hybrid approach that combines 2D animation with computer animation, perhaps giving Disney a venue to keep the nostalgic look of 2D animation alive. Moreover, with Disney’s shaky track record of original animated films in recent years, Lilo & Scratch wisely offers something extra to entice fans to head to theaters for Hexed .

In fact, this trend appears to be experiencing a bit of a resurgence. Warner Bros.’ animated The Cat in the Hat also employed a similar tactic this year, attaching the Looney Tunes short Daffy Season to its theatrical release. With the future of movie theaters perpetually in question, Disney’s decision to use Stitch — by far one of its most popular characters right now — to prop up Hexed is a smart move. Especially given the Disney+ of it all, today’s audiences need an incentive to prioritize seeing a movie in theaters rather than simply waiting for streaming. Lilo & Scratch could be an effective way to address that problem while staying true to Disney’s storied history.

Will you be seeing Hexed (and Lilo & Scratch ) in theaters? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments section below!

Hexed hits theaters everywhere on November 25, 2026.

articles.title: Carrie Coon & Lily James Humanized Cult Member And Leader In Guy Nattiv’s ‘The Liberation’ - Contenders L.A.
articles.summary: Carrie Coon and Lily James grew to understand their roles in the cult thriller The Liberation — compounded by the fact that director Guy Nattiv based the film on his own grandmother. Coon plays Rita, an unhappy woman who finds a place she feels she belongs. Under the mentorship of Ricki King (James), Rita unburdens […]
articles.content:
Carrie Coon and Lily James grew to understand their roles in the cult thriller The Liberation — compounded by the fact that director Guy Nattiv based the film on his own grandmother.

Coon plays Rita, an unhappy woman who finds a place she feels she belongs. Under the mentorship of Ricki King (James), Rita unburdens herself. Eventually, though, Ricki convinces Rita to give her money and divorce her husband. The trio spoke about the film at Deadline's Contenders Film Los Angeles on Saturday.

"I just was so moved by Guy's grandmother's story and the way Guy has humanized every step," Coon said. "We understand just how radical what she's doing is. As a woman, I understand why she might want to cede all agency to someone else. I understand why a patriarchal structure wasn't fulfilling to her." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Coon also called The Liberation a love story between Rita and Ricki. Likewise, James did not want to make Ricki a caricature villain.

"We really wanted to do that to find the total humanity in these women," James said. "It's not the villain. It's so much more complicated. The fact that she could switch from generosity and empathy and love and kindness to savagery and annihilation. When you're out, you're out. Her motivations are so clear. She truly believes she's saving these women. She truly believes she has this power. I could lead with strength."

Nattiv remembered the changes in his grandmother when he was a child. After the real Rita's death, he visited the cult leader and was able to ask some real questions before she expelled him.

"She was miserable and unhappy," the writer-director said. "Then she became happy again. Then she started dancing and started to find herself again, which made sense to us as a family. It didn't make sense when money started disappearing and she was advised to divorce my grandfather and live for good somewhere in America writing postcards. I didn't see my grandmother until after she passed." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Coon's real-life husband, Tracy Letts, plays Rita's husband, Reuben. They have two daughters, played by Bella Ramsey and Odessa Young.

"Who are we to say what someone needs to process their trauma?" Coon said. "We don't get to decide for somebody else. The tragedy and the pain played out in Bella and Odessa and Tracy … you feel the loss. Bella is the cypher for the audience."

The real Rita also was the sole survivor of her family in the Holocaust. Coon studied her testimonies about surviving.

"Speaking the unspeakable is a very challenging act and so many people have to brace themselves," Coon said. "The video gets stopped very frequently. I wanted to dignify that experience because I'm not culturally Jewish. I would never want that to feel not lived in."

The Liberation will have a Oscar-qualifying theatrical run this year and open January 8.

articles.title: One Transformers Fan Just Created a Touching Rolling Tribute to Peter Cullen
articles.summary: Peter Cullen, the legendary voice of Optimus Prime in the Transformers franchise, passed away in August, and now a fan has unveiled a touching rolling tribute. Joe Fiduccia owns Optimus Is Here, the world's first and only replica of the Optimus Prime truck from Transformers: Age of Extinction. Fiduccia considers the truck a rolling tribute […]
articles.content:
In addition, Fiduccia gave the Transformers fans the opportunity to be involved. Alongside the tribute to Cullen, there are 50 stars with initials and dates representing individuals who have passed away, including Fiduccia's mother Judy and Linkin Park's Chester Bennington. The stars were submitted and paid for by the fan community, and all of the funds went to covering the costs associated with the tributes that now adorn the truck, while also “memorializing them forever on a tribute that will be seen by millions around the globe,” Fiduccia said on the Optimus Is Here website .

Built in 2016 with legal permission from Hasbro, Fiduccia began the project to inspire his son. Now, ten years later, what he does has evolved into so much more. His work now inspires millions who follow their journey across social media and generates smiles with every mile. Fiduccia travels the United States and Canada with Optimus Prime. They have appeared at events, granted wishes for Make-A-Wish children, and even escorted a 15-year-old boy who passed away to his final resting place. He also goes to schools for unforgettable anti-bullying presentations, which have been delivered to almost 100,000 students across North America. Fiduccia was in the middle of doing presentations at a school in Indiana when the news broke about Peter Cullen's passing.

“I knew immediately that I wanted to incorporate something on our replica truck in Peter's honor. He deserves that remembrance … and as the owner of what is now a rolling tribute to a beloved character, I have an obligation to fulfill that for him,” Fiduccia said. Throughout their journey, they have added many memorials and tributes to the truck. The side panels on the front bumper feature memorials to the US military and Kyle Comeau, the artist behind Optimus Prime's flames, who passed away before he could work on the screen-used trucks. There are also memorials for children who have passed away that Fiduccia provided with VIP visits, and most recently, the one he escorted in their funeral procession. Now Peter Cullen is memorialized as well. Added to the sleeper cab on November 7th, 2026, the tribute was unveiled to the public on November 12th through a recorded video after he set up for an event in King of Prussia, Pennsylvania.

Honoring a Legacy Image credit: Optimus is here The live-action Transformers films can be quite divisive. Joe Fiduccia often receives comments on social media saying his truck isn't the real Optimus Prime or that it is “just a truck” when people get excited to see it. But the Autobot leader is more than his vehicle mode, and Optimus Is Here is more than just a truck. What truly matters is what the character stands for and what Fiduccia does in representing him. No matter the continuity, Optimus Prime is a character with strong morals. He stands for justice, kindness, and freedom. In his obituary , Peter Cullen's family asked his fans to “honor Peter's remarkable legacy by serving your communities and leading others with compassion, integrity and loyalty and always remembering to, ‘be strong enough to be gentle.'” Cullen embodied the qualities of Optimus Prime.

For Fiduccia, honoring Cullen and his legacy goes beyond just the tributes on his truck's sleeper cab. He will continue using Optimus Prime to inspire the world even more to honor the voice-acting legend . “I don't take what we have lightly. Our replica has never been ‘just a truck' to me. It is a symbol of hope, leadership, and all things that Optimus stood for,” Fiduccia said. “With Peter's passing, it is now my responsibility to continue doing everything in my power to represent this character (and Peter's legacy) in the way they both deserve. I will always try my best, with or without help, and absolutely appreciate the ongoing support from fans around the globe.”

Are you doing anything to honor Peter Cullen? Let us know down in the comments.

articles.title: The VisionQuest Finale Continued a Marvel Trend With Its Big Showdown, and Addressed a Fan Complaint
articles.summary: Courtesy of The Walt Disney Company For a decade, the Marvel Cinematic Universe was the place to go to see bad guys get their comeuppance in a blaze of guns, lazers, and brutal hand-to-hand fights that ended with their demise. After 23 movies of death and destruction, the Infinity Saga ended in 2019 with Spider-Man: Far From Home and something began […]
articles.content:
The MCU has sometimes struggled to find the right balance to please audiences following the unequaled spectacle and story of Avengers: Endgame . The movies that were released in Phase 4 suffered from an expectation that every movie that followed would deliver the same level of action along with the problems faced from the COVID-19 shutdowns. Black Widow, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, Eternals and others all received online criticism from those who declared that Marvel Studios had lost its edge and superhero movies were dead. This was not helped by then-Disney CEO Bob Chapek wanting to push out more content quicker to capitalize on the success of Endgame , which instead led to rushed CGI effects and a feeling that there was just too many superhero movies and TV shows to keep up with. Now, several years down the line, Marvel Studios is ready to release what could be its biggest movie of all time, and VisionQuest is the last project to arrive before Doomsday ‘s December debut .

VisionQuest picks up the final threads of WandaVision to complete the story arc of Vision following his resurrection in the MCU's first TV series. The story finds Vision with his old memories, a host of Tony Stark's old AIs in human avatar form in his own Mindscape…oh, and Ultron, the one-time biggest threat to humanity who now looks like James Spader and can still deliver a withering putdown. The series includes some flawless CGI from Marvel Studios, especially when Ultron returns to his robotic form to take on Vision in the series' final act. VisionQuest's story is always leading to a showdown between Vision and his “father,” and fans got to see the AI punch-up between the androids with all the furniture breaking and brutal body slams any Marvel fan could want. But this moment comes in the middle of the episode, not at the end.

Instead of Vision killing Ultron in some way, this fight leads to Vision coming to realize that the only way he could stop Ultron attempting to kill humanity all over again was to help him talk through the grief of losing his new-found love in fellow AI Jocasta. This becomes one of the defining moments of the series as Vision traps Ultron in “UltraVision,” his own version of WandaVision, where the pair are contained in a sitcom environment to try and work through the issue. This is something that mirrors the way Wanda dealt with her grief in WandaVision , where she eventually came to the realization that she could not maintain the fake life she had created and released everyone under her spell. By the end of VisionQuest , Ultron has been talked down and accepted – for now – that the human race does not need to be destroyed .

The Multiverse Saga has been steering many of its stories away from all villains needing to die and has been trying to put out a message that sometimes you can sit down and rationally work through differences rather than going straight for the jugular with the force of a bazooka. For some people, this was not what they wanted to see and several projects that ended without a big blow out moment were labeled “disappointing” and “boring.” Yet, this kind of ending has become one of the most common in the MCU, with a moment of violence and destruction being countered by a subsequent moment where words are more powerful than weapons. With VisionQuest ‘s final episode, it looks like this is something Marvel Studios is keen to continue with where possible.

While every early MCU ended with violence, the Multiverse Saga has included plenty of movies that end with the villain still alive having been either captured to shown the error of their ways. Spider-Man: No Way Home ended with three versions of Peter Parker helping to “cure” the villains that they had faced across the multiverse, bringing them back from the things that had turned them evil and sending them back to their own universes to face their fate. Guardians of the Galaxy: Vol 3, Captain America: Brave New World, Thunderbolts , and Spider-Man: Brand New Day all followed this new format of giving everyone that big action moment but ultimately trying to get across the message that not everything has to end with a violent resolution. VisionQuest may be the latest to continue this trend, but it is unlikely to be the last.

How have Marvel handled their recent movie endings? Let us know which have worked and which haven't for you in the comments.

articles.title: 5 DC Comics Stories That Took Beloved Superheroes in Directions Fans Still Haven't Forgotten
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics DC Comics is responsible for some of the greatest stories in the history of comics. The publisher created the superhero back in 1938 and since then has been refining the concept, all while branching them out into sci-fi, fantasy, horror, romance, slice of life, and basically every other genre you can imagine. They pushed the […]
articles.content:
Over the years, readers have gotten stories that have run the gamut of quality, from amazing and unforgettable to bad and completely forgettable. However, there's another category. There are some stories that have become so infamous they can't be forgotten. Some of them are bad and some of them are just acquired tastes. These five DC stories became unforgettable, but not always for the best reasons.

Countdown to Final Crisis has been maligned for years , but I remember buying it as it came out, being excited for the weekly issues, at least at the beginning. The weekly series came out in 2007, right as 52 ended, leading to the next big DC event, Final Crisis . The story basically takes readers across the DC Multiverse as the Monitors start hunting down multiversal variants and the New Gods begin their cataclysmic final war, with the heroes trying to figure out exactly what is going on.

Countdown to Final Crisis has its moments (I love all the stuff with Karate Kid, for example, and the Jimmy Olsen stuff is fun too), but what has made it so unforgettable is just how much it bungled everything. See, Final Crisis was written by Grant Morrison and at the time, Morrison wasn't really sharing what they were doing with DC editorial. The creators and editors of Countdown basically went rogue and the series doesn't really actually set up Final Crisis at all. Whether you like it or not, it will always be remembered for not even attempting to live up to its title.

The Dark Knight Returns is one of the greatest moments in comic history. Frank Miller's story about a 50-something Batman taking up the cowl again has gone down as one of the books that helped mature the medium and is on numerous best of all-time lists. It has become a seminal moment in comic history and for many fans it has no equals. It also has no sequels for many fans, despite there being several and The Dark Knight Strikes Again is the reason for that. This was the follow-up to the classic and it's become infamous in its own right.

A lot of people will tell you its terrible, but it isn't. It's actually a pretty good DC story set in a dark alternate future. However, it's the sequel to a comic that many consider to be one of the greatest ever and fans had sky expectations. It didn't reach them, so suddenly it's the worst thing ever. The funny thing is a lot of the things that readers complain about were all done in the original as well. It's a story that is remembered for being terrible, but the truth is a bit more complicated than that.

Heroes In Crisis is legitimately hated by many DC fans . The story introduced readers to the concept of Sanctuary, a place where the heroes could go to deal with their own mental issues. When all of the patients there are killed, with only Booster Gold and Harley Quinn surviving, the superhero community mobilizes to figure out who did it, something made more difficult when the existence of Sanctuary is leaked to the press. The story itself is mostly okay, but the reveal of the killer is what makes the book so hated, as it was revealed that Wally West lost control of his powers and accidentally killed everyone, using time travel to commit suicide out of guilt.

Fans immediately rebelled because they loved Wally. However, I think that this story often gets unfairly maligned. While the mystery is kind of blah and it's a little too long for its own good, the concept of Sanctuary is super-interesting and it makes sense that Wally would be as damaged as he was. It's a story that has its problems but that's the case with most comics, it just had the unfortunate honor of doing something no one liked with a character everyone loved.

Convergence is one of the last major New 52 events. It revolves around Brainiac gaining access to the various dead worlds of the multiverse, stealing cities from each of them, and placing them all on one planet, which would become the living being known as Telos, leading to a war between the various heroes and villains. Convergence is a multiverse story that had very little effect on the overall line of DC books and it came at a time when a lot of fans were checked out of the New 52. It's gone down as a failure, but it's actually remembered with some esteem from fans.

While the main book gets its share of negativity, the tie-ins are pretty universally praised, which is rather unique in the pantheon of events. See, each two-issue miniseries took readers to various fan-favorite Earths, including the post- Crisis Earth. That's right, this is the story that brought back the pre- Flashpoint Superman and Lois Lane, all while introducing the world to Jon Kent. So, while this story isn't particularly loved for what it is and had no effect on anything overall, it birthed the best new DC hero in years and has some excellent tie-in books.

Wonder Woman has starred in awesome stories , but not all of them can be great. In fact, some of them can be downright bad, which leads us to 2007's Amazons Attack! . This story spun out of events in Wonder Woman (Vol. 3), when Diana was imprisoned by the US government, leading Hippolyta and the Amazons to attack Man's World in an effort to free her. The rest of the hero community has to step up to stop one of the most potent fighting forces on Earth, but there's more going on than anyone realizes. Honestly, if you just go by that set-up, this story seems like it should be pretty good, but for whatever reason the execution of it was the main problem.

The story was poo-poo'ed by fans and critics alike and it includes some of the most meme-d moments in DC history. The scene that really stands out involves the Amazons using bees to attack the world and Batman saying, “Bees, my god,” as if it was the most dangerous weapon ever. The story did come out in the aftermath of The Wicker Man remake, so it might have been homaging that, but it was just one of many weird moments that made this story unforgettable for all the wrong reasons.

What DC stories do you remember for the wrong reasons? Any you think deserve to be on the list? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.title: Free Nintendo Switch 2 Upgrades Released for 3 Switch Games
articles.summary: Free Nintendo Switch 2 upgrades have been released for three Nintendo Switch games. In other words, there are three new Nintendo Switch 2 games that are available for free to those who own the previously released Nintendo Switch versions. It's not incredibly rare for free Nintendo Switch 2 upgrades, but it's not common either. To […]
articles.content:
None of the Nintendo Switch 2 games are very expensive, ranging from $15 to $25. If you somehow qualify for all three, though, you are saving a meaningful $65. Meanwhile, some free upgrade paths are restricted to a limited window, but there is no word of that being present here. This trio notably follows a similar free upgrade for a new Sega game .

Herdling is a single-player puzzle game from developer Okomotive and publisher Panic. The former is the studio behind 2018's Far: Lone Sails and 2022's Far: Changing Tides . Upon release, Herdling earned a Metacritic range of 74 to 79. It debuted in 2025.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 version, compared to the previous Nintendo Switch version, has enhanced resolution, increased performance, and greater detail, which results in “a smoother and more beautiful experience.”

Herdling , for those who decide to check it out on Nintendo Switch 2, is roughly three to five hours long and normally costs $25.

Rooftops & Alleys: The Parkour Game is a third-person single-player and multiplayer parkour game from developer MLMedia, which debuted with its release in 2025. It has a Metacritic range of 67 to 70.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 version increases the game's frame rate from 60 to 120, improves the loading times, adds new community-created content, and adds multiplayer crossplay.

Rooftops & Alleys is about four to ten hours long, though its multiplayer component can bring this range up substantially. It normally costs $25.

A Little to the Left is a cozy puzzle game from developer Max Inferno and publisher Secret Mode. It served as the debut release for the former. Upon release, it earned a Metacritic range of 75 to 77. Of the three games here, it is the most popular, but Herdling is probably the best of the three.

The new Nintendo Switch 2 version gives owners higher-resolution graphics, improved frame rates up to 120 fps, faster load times, and adds mouse controls.

A Little to the Left is between four and thirteen hours long, and for this content, Switch 2 users have to fork over $15 to the eShop.

If none of these new releases tickle your Switch 2's fancy, or if you are after something more nostalgic than new, a PS1 exclusive was notably and recently stealth-released on the Switch 2 .

articles.title: Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys' Bass Singer, Dies at 83
articles.summary: Sterban died in Hendersonville, Tennessee, to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the music group announced.
articles.content:
Richard Sterban, the Oak Ridge Boys' bass singer who memorably lent his vocals to their beloved “Elvira” cover, has died. He was 83.

Sterban died Nov. 14 in Hendersonville, Tennessee, due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the Oak Ridge Boys announced.

“We appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers. Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time, we find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus,” Sterban's family said in a statement. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Dawn Greenhalgh, Voice of the Elephant Queen Celeste in 'Babar' Cartoons, Dies at 93 Music Gerry Griffith, Music Executive Who Discovered Whitney Houston, Dies at 87

Born April 24, 1943, in Camden, New Jersey, Sterban began singing at six in Sunday school as a soprano. He sang tenor in his seventh-grade glee club, and upon his eighth grade, his voice dropped to bass.

He studied music at Trenton State College (modernly known as the College of New Jersey), and began singing in a gospel quartet where he met Joe Bonsall, his future Oak Ridge Boys bandmate.

While singing part-time, Sterban joined J.D. Sumner and the Stamps, whom Elvis Presley hired to sing behind him. He then sang and recorded with the King of Rock and Roll, and also appeared in the 1972 concert film Elvis on Tour .

Sterban was then offered the opportunity to join the Oak Ridge Boys after the departure of Noel Fox, which he accepted in 1972. Bonsall joined the group one year later, with Duane Allen, William Lee Golden and Sterban already in the group, which carried on as the faces of the band for five decades.

They performed with Johnny Cash, who helped them sign with Columbia Records in 1973, though it was after opening for Roy Clark in 1975 when they met his manger, Jim Halsey, who would later sign with the group. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

They reached success with "Y'all Come Back Saloon,” which reached No. 3 on the country chart in 1977, and led to a string of hits. "I'll Be True to You” became their first No. 1 song, though 1981's “Elvira” would become one of their largest successes.

Originally recorded by Dallas Frazier, the Oak Ridge Boys' version of the track went to No. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart, sold more than two million copies and won a Grammy. Sterban's bass refrain was a major touchpoint on the song.

The Oak Ridge Boys went on to also become members of the Grand Ole Opry, the Gospel Music Hall of Fame and the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Sterban released his memoir From Elvis to Elvira: My Life on Stage , written with Steven Robinson, in 2012.

Sterban is survived by his wife, Donna; his daughters, Lauren (Tyler) and Tori (Michael); his sons, Rich (Chele), Doug, and Chris; his grandchildren, Mali (Zachary), Nikolas, Tyler (Ryann), Madelyn, Alexandra, Rex, Owen, and Charli Grace; and his great-grandchildren, Salem, Asher, and Theo. He was preceded in death by his mother Victoria Sterban, brother Joseph Sterban and grandson Zachary.

articles.title: James Bond Star's Forgotten 29-Year-Old Disaster Movie is Blowing Up on Free Streaming
articles.summary: Courtesy of Universal There are some actors that are part of a huge franchise that make other movies around the same that then get lost to time. That is true of one 1997 disaster movie as not only was its star better known at the time for recently taking on the role of James Bond but had to […]
articles.content:
Dante's Peak is set in the fictional town of Dante's Peak, Washington, as volcanologist Dr. Harry Dalton (Brosnan) investigates seismic activity occurring inside a long-dormant volcano next to the town. Despite Dalton's warnings of imminent disaster, his worries are dismissed until it is too late and the town is engulfed in lava flows and acrid smoke. With the help of the town's mayor (Hamilton) Dalton must lead an evacuation attempt to escape the continued destruction. The film leads into plenty of the usual tropes – Dalton is haunted by the death of his fiancee in a previous eruption, several stubborn residents refusing to evacuate, last minute escapes – and that didn't help make it stand out with reviewers or in its performance in theaters. Although it marginally won the day over Volcano, Dante's Peak ended up being buried in time.

Pierce Brosnan made his debut as James Bond in GoldenEye in 1995 and followed that up with Tomorrow Never Dies in 1997, in between Dante's Peak was a movie that continued to push the Irish actor as an action hero but the execution of the movie and its extortionate budget did not help it stick in the memory for long. That is probably why the film is perfect for free streaming audiences, as a movie with two big star names attached, an action-packed premise and a non-existent legacy meaning most people have forgotten it even exists. When the movie originally hit cinemas with a colossal $116 million budget (one of the highest ever at the time) it was always going to struggle to make enough money from ticket sales alone to break even. With just $178 million worldwide, the final tally made it a flop, especially when compared to Brosnan's Bond adventures.

Dante's Peak did have an advantage of opening two months before Volcano (although that film did not fare any better on its release) after Universal pumped more money into the visual effects teams in order to get their film on screen first. When it debuted the visual effects were one thing that did their job, but for critics everything else was bad from the dialogue to the chemistry even though it is also regarded as one of the most scientifically accurate disaster movies every made. The film scored just 36% with critics and 39% with audiences, who seemed to be on exactly the same page in their assessment that when things were on fire, the film was great, but the rest of the time it was a bit of an ashy mess. However, this is exactly what free streaming is there for, so that people can reacquaint themselves with movies they would not necessarily pay to see again but pass the time when you don't need to pay for a subscription to watch them.

Which movie was better? Dante's Peak or Volcano ? Let us know in the comments.
